Maya (CS Ops): quick heads up — noticed a spike in playbook misfires this morning when playbooks target account owners. root cause looks like contact_aliases in CRM mapping to multiple contact_ids. proposing to add a canonical_contact_id column and run a dry-run backfill + healthscore recompute on a sampled cohort. :warning:
Jon (Data Eng): do you have a quick example of the alias collision?
Maya (CS Ops): yes — saw cases where same email had two contact_id rows and playbook matched wrong owner. sample row:
```
contact_id | email           | alias_key
-----------+-----------------+---------
102345     | alex@acme.com   | alex_acme_v1
502789     | alex@acme.com   | alex_acme_v2
```
When playbooks run `owner = lookup(contact_id)` they sometimes pick 502789 which is stale.
Jon (Data Eng): got it. canonical_contact_id makes sense. what's the proposed cadence for backfill and recompute?
Maya (CS Ops): plan: 1) create `canonical_contact_id` on staging and prod as nullable; 2) backfill in 5% sample for Saturday with low traffic; 3) recompute healthscore for sampled accounts only and measure delta vs baseline; 4) if deltas < 2% for renewal-risk and onboarding flags, expand to 25% then 100%.
Priya (CS Product): flag — healthscore changes will affect renewal nudge triggers. we should freeze nudge sends for sampled accounts or set a feature flag so nudges are based on pre-change score during experiment. :eyes:
Liam (CS): agree — last time we saw a 6% bump and it triggered extra outreach. freezing nudges is safer.
PlaybookBot: playbook-runner aborted 15:42:17 — duplicate-contact-threshold exceeded for rule owner-claim-v2. Instances affected: 48.
Anita (SRE): resource note — recomputing healthscore for many accounts spikes CPU on metricizer. suggest concurrency cap and run in small batches, e.g., 100 accounts / minute. also add retry/backoff.
Jon (Data Eng): SQL sketch for the canonical mapping (as a starting point):
```sql
-- dedupe by most_recent_activity_ts as canonical
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT contact_id, email, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY LOWER(email) ORDER BY most_recent_activity_ts DESC) AS rn
  FROM crm.contacts
  WHERE email IS NOT NULL
)
UPDATE crm.contacts c
SET canonical_contact_id = r.contact_id
FROM ranked r
WHERE LOWER(c.email) = LOWER(r.email) AND r.rn = 1;
```
Maya (CS Ops): perfect. we'll add a sanity check to ensure canonical_contact_id != contact_id only when we have high confidence. also plan to emit a telemetry metric `cs.canonical.backfill.diff_pct`.
Priya (CS Product): experiment analysis: track these KPIs over sample window — renewal_trigger_rate, onboarding_incomplete_pct, owner_claim_errors. we need a dashboard.
Liam (CS): can we add an idempotency guard to playbooks so they skip if owner claim timestamp < canonical_backfill_ts? that will avoid mid-flight surprises.
Jon (Data Eng): yes, we can add `canonical_backfill_ts` column and playbooks check it. small change in query.
Anita (SRE): recommend running first backfill only against a synthetic subset in staging and validate SLO impact. I'll reserve a maintenance window Saturday 02:00-06:00 UTC for low-priority recompute jobs.
Maya (CS Ops): action items: @Jon implement backfill SQL in staging by EOD Thu; @Anita reserve job window (thanks); @Priya add experiment dashboard and freeze rule for nudges; @Liam coordinate with ops for owner-claim idempotency change. I'll kick off a 5% dry run on Saturday, monitor `cs.canonical.backfill.diff_pct` and `playbook.owner_claim_errors`. If deltas are small -> expand.
Priya (CS Product): noted. will publish dashboard + experiment doc.
Liam (CS): staging dry run looks good to me; will circle back if owners see anomalies. :thumbsup:
Maya (CS Ops): thanks team — will post results in this thread after the dry run. :tada:
